items.definition: The staff member who arranges tickets, tours, taxis, doctors and anything else the hotel does not sell itself.
items.example: The concierge booked a table at a restaurant that was fully booked.

items.definition: A temporary fix that makes a problem go away without solving it.
items.example: We applied a band-aid to the payment process, but the real fix is in the accounting system.

items.definition: A way of working around a problem instead of fixing its cause.
items.example: The manual workaround is for us to check the total by hand every Friday.

items.definition: To return to a topic later. Often used to postpone a decision.
items.example: Let us circle back to the budget question after lunch.

items.definition: To have a short conversation with someone about something.
items.example: Can we touch base on Thursday for fifteen minutes?

items.definition: To move a discussion out of the meeting into a smaller group.
items.example: Let us take this offline and I will send you the figures.

items.definition: To raise an issue or a risk so that people notice it early.
items.example: I want to flag a risk in the schedule before it becomes a problem.

items.definition: To take a matter to a more senior person because it has not moved.
items.example: If we do not hear back by Friday, we will need to escalate this.

items.definition: To give formal permission for something to go ahead.
items.example: Legal has green-lighted the launch for June.

items.definition: The closing line of an email, such as "Kind regards", followed by your name.
items.example: Use a plain sign-off: Kind regards, then your name and title.

items.definition: Agreement and active support for a plan from the people who must carry it out.
items.example: I spent two weeks getting buy-in from the regional teams.

items.definition: A force working against you, such as a rule change or a weak market.
items.example: We are facing a headwind from the new import regulations.

items.definition: The easy results, available with little effort before the harder work.
items.example: We picked the low-hanging fruit first and delivered in three weeks.

items.definition: To increase activity, output or capability, often over a planned period.
items.example: We are ramping up production ahead of the festival season.

items.definition: A long, detailed examination of one subject.
items.example: We did a deep dive on the churn numbers before the review.

items.definition: A rough approximate number, given before the real figure is known.
items.example: Could you give me a ballpark figure for the full build?

items.definition: The capacity a person or team has to take on more work.
items.example: I do not have the bandwidth this week, but I can do it next month.

items.definition: A symbol, often x, whose value is found by solving.
items.example: Let x be the unknown variable.

items.definition: An equation that can be written as ax + b = 0, with a not equal to zero.
items.example: 2x + 3 = 11 is a linear equation in one unknown.

items.definition: How steep the line is; the coefficient of x.
items.example: A horizontal line has slope zero.

items.definition: The word for your mother. Some families say mom or mommy instead.
items.example: My mum is a nurse. She works at a hospital.

items.definition: Your mum's mother or your dad's mother. You often call her grandma.
items.example: My grandmother grows vegetables in the garden.

items.definition: Your mum's sister, or the wife of your uncle. Sometimes a family friend is called an aunt too.
items.example: My aunt lives in Da Nang.

items.definition: A child of your aunt or your uncle. A cousin is like a brother or sister, but not a real one.
items.example: My cousin Mai is my age. We play together every weekend.

items.definition: The word for your mum and your dad together.
items.example: My parents work at the weekend too.

items.definition: The word you say when you meet somebody. You can use it all day long.
items.example: Hello, I am Minh.

items.definition: A short and casual way to say hello, used with people you already know.
items.example: Hi Bao, are you ready?

items.definition: A friendly question you ask after saying hello, to start a small talk.
items.example: Good morning! How are you today?

items.definition: The words you use to tell somebody your own name.
items.example: My name is Lan, and I am seven.

items.definition: What you say the first time you meet somebody. It is polite and warm.
items.example: Nice to meet you. I am Minh.

items.definition: Polite and friendly towards other people, even when you do not like their food.
items.example: It is kind to say thank you for the food.

items.definition: A nice thing you say about what somebody did or made.
items.example: I gave her a compliment about her picture.

items.definition: To ask somebody to join you, and to accept it when they say no.
items.example: I invited him to sit with us.

items.definition: To make room for somebody in the group, the game or the talk.
items.example: We included the new boy in our game.

items.definition: Something done or thought wrongly.
items.example: Use it when a mistake costs time or a retry.

items.definition: To taste a food for the first time. One small bite is enough for today.
items.example: I will try one bite of the soup.

items.definition: To make something right or better after it went wrong.
items.example: I fixed the picture with a new sheet of paper.

items.definition: To say sorry and show that you understand what you did wrong.
items.example: I apologised to my sister for shouting.

items.definition: A small mistake that happens because you were busy or in a hurry.
items.example: That was just a slip.

items.definition: The one you like most of all, the one you hope to see on the table.
items.example: My favourite food is spring rolls.
